A `DatePickerPreset` picks its `value` and closes the popup. It shows as pressed while its value is selected.

A controller from `createDatePickerController()` sets the date or opens the calendar from anywhere, and `onValueChange` reports each change. Leave `value` unset here, so the calendar can move to the month the controller picks.

The calendar opens as a dialog with a grid of days, each named in full, like “Friday, November 20, 2026”. The hint describes the input, so screen readers hear the format to type. Text that isn’t a date sets `aria-invalid` and keeps the old value, and unavailable days stay focusable so keyboard users still hear them.
The size of each day, larger on touch screens.

The trigger, popup and arrows have English names. Pass `aria-label` to each to translate them. Inputs use a 16px font on touch screens so iOS doesn’t zoom, and the popup only scales in when motion is allowed.
UI SDK adds a little CSS of its own in a cascade layer named `ui-sdk`. Declare that layer at the top of your global stylesheet, above the Tailwind import, so your classes win over it.

Values are ISO date strings like `2026-11-20`, with no time or time zone, so you don’t need a date library. People type in their own date order, like 11/20/2026 or 20.11.2026, and the field formats the date when they press Enter or leave it. `DatePickerContent` with no children renders a styled calendar.
With `mode="range"`, add a second input with `end`. The calendar stays open after the first date and closes after the second. `months={2}` shows two months side by side, stacked on small screens.
With a `name`, the date submits as an ISO string. `required` blocks an empty submit, text that isn’t a date blocks one too, and reset goes back to `defaultValue`.
With an Arabic locale inside dir=rtl, the field, the arrows and the calendar all run from the right.
`disabled` stops typing and opening. `readOnly` still opens the calendar so people can look, but nothing can change.
`locale` sets the typed format, the hint and the calendar’s names. Without it, the picker reads the page’s `lang`. The buttons have English names, so pass `aria-label` to translate them.
`min`, `max` and `unavailable` apply to typing and picking. Here weekends and two holidays can’t be picked, and a typed one is marked invalid.
